facts.fact: GabonReview reports that workshops opened at Ntoum on 23 June 2025 to draw up a roadmap and action plan described as a preliminary to the effective start of three projects, among them the Centre national d'état civil (CNEC); the workshops were also to map the civil status centres. The project had therefore not started.
GabonReview states the three projects, including the CNEC, are financed by the World Bank under the Gabon Digital programme, component 2.

The secretary-general of the Interior ministry is reported as placing the three projects, including the CNEC, in the continuation of the Plan national de développement pour la transition 2024-2026, which makes legal and digital identification a lever of administrative transformation; the article does not say the plan names the CNEC.

systems.owner: Gabon Digital programme, component 2 (general coordinator: ANINF deputy director-general); Ministry of the Interior, Security and Decentralisation
systems.tiers: not started as of June 2025; civil status centres to be mapped
existing system to be inventoried, with CNIE, CNAMGS, CNSS and DGDI

systems.system: Common biometric reference (interconnection of RBPP, SNID and CNEC)
systems.tiers: ambition: to interconnect the three systems

note: The article describes the CNEC thinly, as the civil registration pillar of an integrated identification ecosystem; it is classed civil on that and on the mapping of civil status centres.
